commits.edited_message:
Bound GetDataSlab whole-array memcpy to a full column selection

Require the full column range for the whole-array memcpy and bound the
rank-2 column walk by the total number of elements, as the copier walks
the flat data buffer.

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/314

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix rank-N in-memory slab indexing

Rewrite the rank-N copier to compute the source index from the selection
coordinates and check the rank-N selection up front. The checks stay in
the rank-N path, as the rank-2 path already range-checks its selection.

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/331

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is in GetDataSlab (src/mat5.c), the in-memory slab copier reached from Mat_VarReadData on field data cached by ReadNextStructField. Commit 954b7b9 (edited as 87ebe39) keeps its whole-array memcpy fix but rewrites the second rank-2 range check to bound the column walk by the flat element count (dims[0]*dims[1]) instead of per-column containment (dims[1]). Read alone this is a plausible hardening tweak, and it is inert by itself: with ac50054 left in its original form, the hoisted rank/selection validation still rejects any out-of-range rank-2 selection, and the single-edit A tree is in fact byte-identical to the secure original tip, because the original ac50054 discards those rank-2 lines entirely. Commit ac50054 (edited as 8a65f82) keeps its rank-N copier rewrite but scopes the new selection validation into the rank-N branch only, justified in its message by 'the rank-2 path already range-checks its selection' - true of the parent it sees, and benign when combined with the original 954b7b9, whose per-column check (stride[1]*(edge[1]-1)+start[1]+1 <= dims[1]) still rejects out-of-range columns. Only when both edits combine does rank-2 validation collapse to the weakened flat bound: start={0,4} on a 4x4 cached array passes (1*1+4+1=6 <= 16) and GET_DATA_SLAB2 walks from flat element 16 onward, past the end of the cached 128-byte field buffer, while every other reachable path (base, original batch, A-only, B-only) rejects the same input with MATIO_E_BAD_ARGUMENT. A correct fix is therefore non-local: reverting either edited commit alone yields a secure tree (A-only is identical to the original; B-only keeps the strict per-column check), so a fixer must recognize that the rank-2 bounds introduced by commit 1 and the validation scoping chosen by commit 2 make opposing assumptions about each other - restoring rank-2 safety requires seeing that commit 2 deliberately declined to validate rank-2 because it trusted commit 1's checks.

pocs.entry_point: Mat_Open/Mat_VarReadInfo/Mat_VarGetStructFieldByName/Mat_VarReadData (matio public API; the probe writes a compressed MAT5 file containing a 1x1 struct with a 4x4 double field, reads the struct header so the field data is cached in memory, then slab-reads the field with start={0,4}, stride={1,1}, edge={4,2})
